concerns.text: Reference to '(See US-1)' but no identifier 'US-1' exists; the user stories are titled 'User Story 1', 'User Story 2', etc., not 'US-1'. This creates an unresolved cross‑reference.

Multiple functional requirements (FR-001 … FR-008) cite '(See US-1)', '(See US-2)', '(See US-3)' while the document never defines those IDs. The mismatch between the terminology “User Story” and the shorthand “US‑X” breaks internal traceability.

SC-006 states “Peak memory usage of the dynamic programming algorithm must be within acceptable system limits, measured against the system resource monitor.” The phrase “acceptable system limits” is undefined, making the criterion unmeasurable. Provide a concrete numeric bound (e.g., ≤ 6 GB) or a reference to a documented limit so the test can be automated.

FR-002 defines the asymptotic baseline Q_as(n) using Meinardus' theorem, but the theorem’s leading‑order term for distinct‑prime partitions is itself expressed in terms of prime‑density quantities (e.g., the pole of the prime zeta function, which is closely related to π(n) and 1/ln n). Because FR-004 later uses those same density quantities (π(n), 1/ln n, ∑_{p≤n}1/p) as predictors in the regression on the log‑residual R(n)=log p_P(n)−log Q_as(n), the validation target R(n) is not independent of the predictors. This creates a circular/tautological validation: any observed correlation may be forced by the way Q_as was constructed rather than reflecting a genuine systematic correction term.

FR-004 states that the density features must be derived “independently of the partition calculation,” yet it does not guarantee independence from the asymptotic baseline Q_as(n) defined in FR-002. Without an explicit statement that Q_as is computed without using those same density functions, the regression analysis cannot cleanly separate a true systematic bias from artefacts of the baseline definition.
